The stack trace code called back into RCU which then called the stack trace again."

commit 2a820bf74918d61ea54f7c1001f4a6a2e457577c
Author: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Apr 25 11:45:14 2019 +0200

    tracing: Use percpu stack trace buffer more intelligently
    
    The per cpu stack trace buffer usage pattern is odd at best. The buffer has
    place for 512 stack trace entries on 64-bit and 1024 on 32-bit. When
    interrupts or exceptions nest after the per cpu buffer was acquired the
    stacktrace length is hardcoded to 8 entries. 512/1024 stack trace entr
bic_trace_step.reason: The code after this commit implements a nesting mechanism with a maximum of 4 levels (FTRACE_KSTACK_NESTING). It increments a per-CPU counter to select a dedicated stack slot, and if the count exceeds the nesting limit (stackidx > 4), the function bails out via WARN_ON_ONCE and goto out, thus preventing infinite recursion. This addresses the root cause vulnerability (lack of recursion protection) by limiting recursive depth.
